What happens to my GitHub when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 16 Nov 2026

Short answer: GitHub says it can work with an authorised person to decide what happens to a deceased user's account content. Next of kin, a pre-designated successor or another authorised individual (GitHub says this could include a collaborator or business partner) contacts GitHub Support, for example to transfer public repositories or cancel billing. If you appoint a successor in advance, they can archive or transfer your public repositories after presenting a death certificate and waiting 7 days, or an obituary and waiting 21 days. Successors can't log into your account.

Key facts

  • Successors can archive or transfer public repositories
  • Successors cannot log into your account
  • Successor wait: 7 days with a death certificate, 21 days with an obituary
  • Requests go through the GitHub Support portal

How do I prepare my GitHub account?

  1. Invite a successor: click your profile picture, then Settings, then Account. Under 'Successor settings', type their username, full name or email, select them and click Add successor. They need a GitHub account and show as 'Pending' until they agree.
  2. Back up what matters yourself. GitHub's docs describe a mirror clone (git clone --mirror) that keeps the full revision history, plus git lfs fetch --all for Large File Storage objects; wikis can be cloned the same way. Store the archives on an external drive or cloud storage.
  3. Write down your GitHub username, which repositories matter (especially private ones, because GitHub's listed successor permissions cover public repositories) and whether each should be archived, transferred or deleted.
  4. After a death: the successor, next of kin or other authorised person opens the GitHub Support portal, clicks Contact us and gives their name and contact details, the deceased's name and GitHub username, their relationship (and, if a designated successor, their own username) and the action they want.
  5. Expect GitHub to ask for more: a copy of your photo ID, a copy of the death certificate and documents showing you're authorised to act for the account.
  6. If you're the appointed successor, you can manage the public repositories 7 days after presenting a death certificate, or 21 days after presenting an obituary.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Your name and contact information
  • The deceased's name and GitHub username
  • Your relationship to them, and whether you're their designated successor (with your own GitHub username)
  • The action you want, such as transferring public repositories or cancelling billing
  • If GitHub asks: photo ID, a copy of the death certificate and proof you're authorised to act

How long does it take?

An appointed successor can manage public repositories 7 days after presenting a death certificate, or 21 days after presenting an obituary. GitHub publishes no processing time for other requests and may follow up for more information.

What can't be recovered?

  • Account login: GitHub says successors cannot log into the account
  • Private repositories you haven't backed up or shared: GitHub's successor permissions only list public repositories, so keep your own copies

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my GitHub when I die?

GitHub says it can work with an authorised person to decide what happens to a deceased user's account content. Next of kin, a pre-designated successor or another authorised individual (GitHub says this could include a collaborator or business partner) contacts GitHub Support, for example to transfer public repositories or cancel billing. If you appoint a successor in advance, they can archive or transfer your public repositories after presenting a death certificate and waiting 7 days, or an obituary and waiting 21 days. Successors can't log into your account.

What happens to my GitHub account when I die?

GitHub works with an authorised person, such as next of kin or a successor you appointed, to decide what happens to the account's content. They contact GitHub Support with the deceased's username and the action they want, such as transferring public repositories or cancelling billing.

What can a GitHub successor do?

Archive your public repositories, transfer them to their own personal account, or transfer them to an organization where they can create repositories. Successors cannot log into your account.

How long does a GitHub successor have to wait?

7 days after presenting a death certificate, or 21 days after presenting an obituary.

Who can contact GitHub about a deceased user?

Next of kin, a pre-designated successor or another authorised individual, which GitHub says could include a collaborator or business partner. GitHub may ask for photo ID, a death certificate and proof of authority.

How do I back up my GitHub repositories?

GitHub's docs describe a mirror clone (git clone --mirror) that keeps the revision history, plus git lfs fetch --all for Large File Storage objects. Compress the clone and store it somewhere safe, such as an external drive or cloud storage.
